claim: Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_5\) be the five pairwise nonisomorphic asymmetric cubic Hamiltonian graphs on twelve vertices, represented respectively by graph6 strings K?ABE`Ke@WEO, K?ABCfCU@WF?, K?ABAdgi?wQ_, K?AB?tos@WP_, and K?`@EaKX?sEO, and equip each graph with its unweighted shortest-path metric. For the inclusive Vietoris--Rips filtration, all five complexes are twelve discrete points for \(0\le r<1\). For \(1\le r<2\), their homotopy types are respectively \(\bigvee^6S^1,\bigvee^6S^1,\bigvee^5S^1,\bigvee^6S^1,\bigvee^4S^1\). For \(2\le r<3\), the homotopy type is \(\bigvee^2S^2\) for \(G_1\) and \(S^2\) for each of \(G_2,\ldots,G_5\). For every graph the complex is contractible for \(r\ge3\).

correctness.rationale: The five graph6 representatives are replayed exactly. A standalone exhaustive verifier proves each is connected, cubic, Hamiltonian, asymmetric, and pairwise nonisomorphic; reconstructs every Rips simplex at all changing thresholds; verifies complete Hasse diagrams; and checks acyclicity of the stated discrete-Morse matchings. Critical-cell counts imply the exact wedge or contractible homotopy types. The only external premise used for class exhaustion is the published statement that exactly five such isomorphism classes exist.
